I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the crop pattern I know best and trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is the main local system there, with most fields in this rotation and summer rain doing more of the work for maize while wheat needs more irrigation ([Scientific Reports](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep41587), [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/13/9/2362)). I am 55, I have no reason to chase a complicated cash-crop plan this year, and I care first about a steady harvest, manageable labor, and not overspending on water and fertilizer. So I will keep all my land in the wheat-maize rotation, use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put more water and fertilizer into wheat than maize, and keep pest control to a practical number of sprays instead of spraying too often.

I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, irrigate wheat more because spring is drier, rely more on summer rain for maize, and keep fertilizer at a solid but not excessive level so I can control costs and still aim for stable yields.
